neighbours.label: weak unit (max 5.8): the point where a sentence's main clause resumes after its subject was interrupted by an embedded clause or phrase (the comma or verb after 'The X, where ..., '); plain subject-verb sentences stay low
fire: The lake, where the villagers fish every morning, is almost frozen now.
The bridge, which was built by the Romans, is still used by farmers.
The castle, perched on a rocky hill above the town, has been empty for decades.
The museum, where the treaty was signed, is open only in summer.
Our neighbour, a retired pilot from Lisbon, has lived here for years.
The forest, where the old mill once stood, is now a nature reserve.
The temple, located just outside the city walls, was rebuilt in 1820.
The harbour, where the ferries dock at night, is busy all year.
quiet: The lake is almost frozen now, and the villagers fish there every morning.
The Romans built the old bridge, and farmers still use it today.
The castle has been empty for decades and sits on a rocky hill.
The museum is open only in summer because of the heating costs.
Our neighbour is a retired pilot who grew up in Lisbon.
The forest is now a nature reserve with an old mill inside it.
The temple was rebuilt in 1820 after a long fire.
The harbour is busy all year with ferries and fishing boats.

short: main verb resuming after an interrupted subject
notes: Card: weak, peaks on ' is'/' was'/' has' after subjects with embedded material ('Mt. Zozusan, where it is located, is', 'The site, near ... Burgos, has', 'what the document is for'). Probe: 'The mountain, where the shrine is located, is' 0.605, 'what the document is for' 0.308, 'The site, near the old city, has' 0.259; 'That novel is my favourite' 0.052, 'The people of the valley are' 0.064, garden 0.034.
